unproven: Unchanged and still INFRA-63's, since no pod in Legion reaches a cluster or the consuming stack's state: Tailscale Serve resolving the app's cluster DNS name under TS_USERSPACE=true; the cutover's two tailscaled processes against one state Secret, with the consuming program still minting the tailnet key Reusable: false; the front door's unmeasured 100m/128Mi reservation; and whether a release loses no request, which is what decides whether five seconds of pre-stop wait is the right number.

The reviewer's own minor stands and is in the body's risk line: 35 s is a floor rather than a cover, because the kubelet charges the hook's elapsed time — the sleep plus the CRI exec overhead — against the one grace period, so envoy-dispatch gets a little under 30 s where the base gave a flat 30 s. The design's five-second reserve absorbs it and the tightest pinned case is the 27 s lock, leaving roughly 3 s minus that overhead; nothing here measures it.
observations: The guard is the right shape for the hazard it replaces: it lives in the module that owns stopGrace, reads the rendered pod as data rather than mirroring a number, and fails loudly rather than skipping when the golden's shape changes — so the next person to move either value meets it in `envoy-go` instead of discovering it in production. The tester's own inequality test in the infra module still mirrors 30 by hand, which the reviewer batched into the fast-follow; with this guard in place that mirror can go whenever those files are next touched.
